sections.heading: The legal rule
sections.body:
345. (1) A mark used for denoting that movable property belongs to a particular person is called a property mark
(2) Whoever marks any movable property or goods or any case, package or other receptacle containing movable property or goods, or uses any case, package or other receptacle having any mark thereon, in a manner reasonably calculated to cause it to be believed that the property or goods so marked, or any property or goods contained in any such receptacle so marked, belong to a person to whom they do not belong, is said to use a false property mark
(3) Whoever uses any false property mark shall, unless he proves that he acted without intent to defraud, be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both

Step 2 — State the legal test in your own words, then list the ingredients:

enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 345 constitutes a key component of Chapter XVIII (Of Offences Relating to Documents and to Property Marks) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, addressing property mark. The provision balances personal liberty with public interest and social order. The prosecution must establish every statutory element beyond reasonable doubt: the specified actus reus, the requisite mens rea, and any relevant statutory circumstances. Modern judicial interpretation emphasizes substantive fairness, proportionality in sentencing, and adherence to constitutional safeguards. Where statutory exceptions or provisos are attached to the section, the accused must establish facts bringing the case within such provisions under evidentiary standards.
examples: Teaching example (Standard application): An individual intentionally commits acts satisfying the statutory formula of property mark under Section 345 without lawful authority. The individual is liable under BNS s. 345.

Teaching example (Absence of mens rea / Lawful exception): A person acts in good faith or without the requisite statutory mental element under circumstances recognized by law. The essential ingredients of Section 345 are not satisfied; no penal liability attaches.
distinctions: Section 345 vs General Attempt: Section 345 penalizes the substantive conduct specified in Chapter XVIII; inchoate attempts without specific provisions fall under the general attempt provisions.

Section 345 vs Cognate Chapter Offences: Liability under Section 345 is distinguished by its specific mental threshold and the particular legal interest protected under Of Offences Relating to Documents and to Property Marks.
